title: Select and document the AirNow endpoint(s) to call
description:
The API Fact Sheet enumerates several web services with meaningful differences, and the design has been loosely referencing 'currentobservation/latLong' without confirming it's the right one:

  - Current Observations by Reporting Area -- 'Real-time air quality observations (NowCast AQI) for each pollutant measured by reporting areas -- cities or other reporting areas DEFINED BY AIR QUALITY AGENCIES.' Appears to match our needs on all three axes: NowCast, per-pollutant breakdown (widget scope), and reporting-area scoping.
  - Observations by Monitoring Site -- site-level rather than aggregated.
  - Forecasts / Historical Observations by Reporting Area / Contour Maps -- not v1.

Confirm which endpoint actually returns: (a) NowCast AQI, (b) the full per-pollutant breakdown the widget scope requires, (c) the owning agency name for attribution, and (d) a category descriptor, or whether we derive the category from the value against the TAD table (allowed -- that's classification of a received AQI, not computing an AQI; distinct from bluegull-aqi-10h.17).

The 'reporting areas defined by air quality agencies' phrasing is likely where attribution comes from -- airnow.gov showed 'San Francisco Reporting Area' and 'Data courtesy of Bay Area Air District' together. Feeds directly into bluegull-aqi-10h.15. Record the answer in doc/DESIGN.md.
close_reason:
RESOLVED with live-verified evidence, not just documentation reading. The 'classic' endpoint (/aq/observation/latLong/current/) most training data/tutorials reference is being retired by EPA on 2026-09-30 -- found via a dated, merged pyairnow PR migrating for exactly this reason, confirmed directly against EPA's own official PDF notice (AirNowAPIUpdates2026June.pdf), then confirmed live with an actual test query.

Correct endpoint: GET https://www.airnowapi.org/aq/observation/current/ziplatlong/ (?format=application/json&latitude={lat}&longitude={lon}&API_KEY={key}). Response: JSON array, one object per pollutant: dateObserved, hourObserved (string 'HH:MM'), localTimeZone, reportingAreaName, siteID, siteName, parameterName, nowcastAQI, aqiCategoryName, reportingAgency, lookupBehavior, consideredMonitors, lookupBoundary. Error shape: {"WebServiceError":[{"Message":"..."}]}. Empty array = no data.

Answers all four original questions: (a) NowCast AQI -- yes, nowcastAQI field. (b) full per-pollutant breakdown -- yes, one array entry per pollutant. (c) owning agency name for attribution -- yes, reportingAgency field, confirmed present and populated ('Bay Area Air District') in a live response, directly answering bluegull-aqi-10h.15 with no fallback needed for the common case. (d) category descriptor -- yes, aqiCategoryName (no numeric Category.Number in the raw response, unlike the retiring endpoint -- derive the number from the TAD table if needed, that's classification of a received value, not computing an AQI, per bluegull-aqi-10h.17).

Recorded in doc/DESIGN.md 'Backend service' architecture section since both the backend (bluegull-aqi-q9r.2) and AirNowDirectClient need this same endpoint.

title: Never derive AQI client-side; display values as received
description:
HARD CONSTRAINT from two independent sources. The AirNow Data Exchange Guidelines require data be 'disseminated as received' without alteration. The TAD independently states it is 'not valid to use shorter-term (e.g. hourly) data to calculate an AQI value.'

So: display AirNow's AQI values exactly as returned. NEVER convert a pollutant concentration into an AQI, never re-derive, never interpolate, never round differently than received. The TAD's breakpoint table (Table 5) and interpolation formula (Equation 1) are in the design doc as documentation of what NOT to implement -- they are the agency-side calculation, not ours.

If the API returns a raw concentration for some pollutant WITHOUT an accompanying AQI value, display the concentration labeled as a concentration (with units) -- do not compute an index from it.

Include a test asserting no AQI-derivation logic exists in the codebase (e.g. no breakpoint table, no interpolation against one), so this can't be reintroduced later by someone trying to 'fill in' a missing value. See doc/DESIGN.md 'AQI Technical Assistance Document & API Fact Sheet -- review findings'.
close_reason: Added ComplianceTests.swift: scans every .swift file under Sources/ (comments stripped) for identifiers that would only appear in client-side AQI derivation (breakpoint, interpolat, computeAQI, deriveAQI, calculateAQI, etc). Verified the guard actually works by temporarily injecting a computeAQI function, confirming the test failed, then restoring the file -- not just that it passes on innocent code. The substantive constraint (never derive/re-derive an AQI) was already satisfied by construction from bluegull-aqi-10h.2: AQICategory.init(aqi:) only consumes AirNow's own nowcastAQI value, and PollutantReading has no concentration/breakpoint field to derive from in the first place. 16/16 tests pass via swift test.

title: Round coordinates client-side before transmission
description:
Privacy by design, and free. The service otherwise receives precise coordinates and logs requests, accumulating 'IP X was at location Y at time Z' in CloudWatch for the whole retention period -- an inadvertent location-history database, and a poor fit for an app whose purpose is local environmental data.

AirNow resolves to the nearest monitoring station regardless, so ~1km precision loses no accuracy AND improves cache hit rates. Round before the request leaves the Mac so the server never receives a precise location at all. Applies to both Direct and Service mode.
close_reason: Location.rounded rounds to ~1km precision (2 decimal degrees), deliberately matching the server's LOCATION_KEY_PRECISION in cache.py exactly for cache-hit-rate alignment, not just privacy. AirNowDirectClient rounds before building the request -- AirNow never receives a precise coordinate regardless of caller precision; returned AQIReading.location is the rounded value too. Added a note to bluegull-aqi-10h.4 (BluegullServiceClient, not yet built) so the same treatment isn't missed there. Updated two existing tests that asserted exact unrounded coordinates, added a new rounding-correctness test (not just truncation) at a .5 boundary. 61/61 tests pass via swift test.

title: Add cost circuit breakers: reserved concurrency + API Gateway throttling
description:
Denial of wallet is the primary threat on this architecture. Lambda, API Gateway, and on-demand DynamoDB all scale elastically, so they all BILL elastically -- a sustained flood costs money at a rate nothing in the base design bounds. Per-IP WAF rate limiting does little against a botnet, and WAF bills per request itself, amplifying cost under attack rather than capping it.

  - Lambda reserved concurrency: a hard ceiling on concurrent executions and therefore on cost per unit time. This is the PRIMARY circuit breaker, not just a noisy-neighbor courtesy -- note the existing scale-config task frames it that way and should be read together with this one.
  - API Gateway stage throttling: hard request-rate cap, independent of WAF.
  - DynamoDB on-demand has no ceiling by design; the Lambda cap is what indirectly bounds it.
close_reason: Added LambdaReservedConcurrentExecutions parameter (default 20, conservative for a project sharing this AWS account with Plant-Tracer) wired to AqiFunction.ReservedConcurrentExecutions -- the primary denial-of-wallet circuit breaker. Added ApiThrottlingRateLimit/ApiThrottlingBurstLimit (defaults 10/20) wired to AqiHttpApi.DefaultRouteSettings, independent of WAF (not deployed yet) and of the Lambda ceiling. All three are SAM Parameters, adjustable per environment via parameter_overrides without a code change. sam validate --lint and sam build both succeed; 35/35 tests still pass (no code changes, template-only).

title: Validate coordinates and reject out-of-coverage requests
description:
Closes the cache-cardinality attack, which the stampede mitigation does NOT cover: stale-while-revalidate + single-flight collapses concurrent requests for the SAME key, so an attacker requesting a million DISTINCT coordinates produces a million cache misses, each triggering an upstream AirNow call -- burning the AirNow quota (likely getting the key banned), filling DynamoDB with junk, and running up Lambda cost.

Required:
  - Validate lat/long are numeric, in range, and sanely bounded.
  - Reject coordinates outside AirNow's coverage area BEFORE any upstream call. A request for the middle of the Pacific should cost a 400, not an AirNow request.
  - Snap to a coarse grid so total cache key cardinality is finite and bounded.
close_reason: Implemented in coverage.py: validate_coverage() rejects physically invalid coordinates and anything outside a generous North America bounding box (CONUS/Alaska/Hawaii/Puerto Rico/Canada/Mexico) before aqi_lookup.get_aqi() even instantiates the cache client -- closes the cardinality-attack gap that stale-while-revalidate/single-flight (q9r.15) doesn't cover. Cache-key grid-snapping was already done via cache.location_key()'s 2-decimal rounding (q9r.2). Fixed two pre-existing tests that used non-North-American coordinates (London; a point south of the box). Verified live via make run-local against the real AirNow API: valid US location succeeded, Pacific/Europe/out-of-range-latitude all returned 400 with no AirNow call or cache-log line. 35/35 tests pass, pylint 10.00/10.

title: Use GitHub Actions OIDC role assumption for AWS deploys
description: Assume an AWS role via OIDC rather than storing long-lived access keys in GitHub secrets -- no durable credential exists to leak, and access is scoped and auditable. Requires an IAM role with a trust policy for GitHub's OIDC provider, restricted to this repo.

title: Redact AirNow keys and raw coordinates before logging
description:
TWO separate leaks, same discipline.

1. CREDENTIAL. AirNow passes its API key as a URL query parameter (...&API_KEY=...), so logging the request URL writes the key straight into CloudWatch Logs, readable by anyone with log access for the whole retention period. This is the likeliest way this project leaks a key and it looks exactly like ordinary debug logging.

2. PRIVACY. Logging raw coordinates accumulates 'IP X was at location Y at time Z' for the retention period -- an inadvertent location-history database. Clients round coordinates before sending (see the client-side rounding task), but the service must not log even rounded values at full fidelity or tie them to source IPs.

Also ensure error responses and stack traces never echo the upstream URL or request headers back to clients. Needs a test asserting neither the key nor raw coordinates appear in log output.
close_reason: Implemented: AirNow key never passed to a logger (only the static base URL and status codes are logged); location keys logged only as a one-way sha256 digest via cache.hash_location_key(), used in cache.py, aqi_lookup.py, and lambda_handler.py's AirNowError path. Also fixed a related gap: logging.basicConfig was setting root level from LOG_LEVEL, which unmuted botocore's own DEBUG logging (raw DynamoDB item bodies) -- root now pinned at WARNING, only the app logger tree honors LOG_LEVEL. 7 new tests in test_logging_redaction.py, verified live via make run-local under LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG. 21/21 tests pass, pylint 10.00/10.

title: Add gitleaks pre-commit hook and CI scan
description:
Two layers: a pre-commit hook catches a secret locally before a commit exists (cheapest possible point), and a CI job backstops commits made without the hook installed -- fresh clones, other machines, other agents.

CRITICAL -- must include a CUSTOM RULE for the AirNow key. GitHub's push protection and gitleaks' default rules both key on distinctive credential formats (AWS 'AKIA...', GitHub 'ghp_...', Stripe 'sk_live_...'). The AirNow key has no such distinctive prefix -- like most government API keys it is a generic token -- so NO pattern scanner will reliably catch a bare one. Default protection therefore covers the AWS and Apple credentials in our inventory but NOT the project's primary secret.

The custom rule must key on context rather than the token shape: assignments to AIRNOW_API_KEY / API_KEY, and any high-entropy token appearing near 'airnowapi.org'. Without this, the layered enforcement described in doc/DESIGN.md has a hole exactly where it matters most.
close_reason: Implemented with Betterleaks (gitleaks' actively-developed drop-in-compatible successor -- gitleaks itself is now feature-complete/maintenance-only, confirmed via web research after Steve flagged its README warning). .betterleaks.toml extends the default ruleset with two custom rules keyed on context (AIRNOW_API_KEY/API_KEY assignment, and a token following API_KEY= on a line containing airnowapi.org) since the AirNow key has no distinctive prefix for shape-based detection. Verified rules against real/placeholder values via betterleaks stdin and against the full repo git history (zero false positives, zero pre-existing leaks). Local hook wired into .beads/hooks/pre-commit (not a separate pre-commit-framework config, which conflicts with Beads already owning core.hooksPath -- confirmed by trying it and reading the refusal). CI backstop added at .github/workflows/secret-scan.yml, pinned to v1.7.2 with checksum verification, dry-run tested locally. Verified live end-to-end: staged fake AIRNOW_API_KEY value was blocked by the hook; clean commit still succeeded.

title: Implement perf baseline storage and regression gate
description:
Two independent checks per metric: an ABSOLUTE ceiling and a RELATIVE regression gate. They catch different failures -- the relative gate catches a sudden jump but is blind to the ratchet (drift 4% eleven times and you've doubled without ever failing a build); the absolute ceiling stops that.

Absolute ceilings (server-side latency, measured API Gateway receive -> response send):
  - Warm cached round-trip: p95 < 50ms, p50 < 25ms
  - Uncached round-trip, AirNow stubbed: p95 < 100ms
  - Cold start Init Duration: p50 < 600ms, investigate > 1s
  - p95 latency at 100 concurrent: within 2x the 10-concurrent p95
  - Error rate at 10 and 100 concurrent: < 0.1%
  - Cache hit ratio under steady-state load: > 95%

Relative gates: 5% on everything except cold start (~15%, variance is inherently larger). Compare percentiles over N>=100 samples, never single measurements.

Baseline lives in perf-baseline.json committed to the repo, so regressions appear as a reviewable diff and accepting an intentional regression is an explicit commit rather than a silent overwrite. Real end-to-end uncached latency (live AirNow) is recorded for observability but NOT gated -- it mostly measures AirNow, which we don't control. Client-observed latency likewise tracked but not gated (DNS/TLS/distance dominate; no code change fixes them).

title: Add AirNow stub/test mode for load testing
description: MANDATORY before any load test runs, not an optimization: driving 100 concurrent uncached requests at the live AirNow API would burn the project's quota and plausibly violate its terms. Env-gated test mode (or a reserved synthetic location) on the dev stage returns canned data in place of the upstream call, so load tests measure our overhead without touching AirNow.
close_reason: New airnow_stub.py gates canned data on BOTH AIRNOW_STUB_MODE=1 AND the reserved synthetic coordinate (40.0, -100.0) -- either alone is not enough, so a real request can never accidentally get stubbed and the reserved coordinate behaves normally when the env var is unset. Deliberately not a template.yaml env var so it can't be baked into a deployed stack by accident; enabling it for an actual load test run is out-of-band, out of this task's scope. Wired into aqi_lookup.get_aqi() so stub responses still flow through the real cache path (only the AirNow HTTP call is replaced) and key resolution is skipped for stub requests. Verified live via make run-local: fresh miss served from stub with a distinct log line, then cache hit; same coordinate without the env var correctly falls through to a real AirNow call. 42/42 tests pass, pylint 10.00/10.

title: Test concurrent cache-miss behavior against DynamoDB Local
description: Verify the stampede mitigation actually works: concurrent misses on the same key must produce exactly one upstream AirNow call, and an expired entry must be served immediately rather than blocking. Runs against DynamoDB Local -- no AWS needed.
close_reason: Added test_concurrent_cache.py: real threading.Thread-based races (not a simulated lock like the rest of test_aqi_lookup.py) verifying concurrent cache misses on the same key produce exactly one AirNow call, and that an expired entry is served immediately rather than blocking behind the request revalidating it. This is deliberately the kind of test that would have caught the two real concurrency bugs found and fixed in q9r.15 (a PutItem-clears-the-lock race and a TOCTOU gap between miss-check and lock-acquisition), both of which were only actually caught via live testing against a real ThreadingHTTPServer, not by simulated-lock unit tests.

title: Implement stale-while-revalidate + single-flight cache logic
description: The core horizontal-scaling mechanism. On a miss against an expired entry: serve the stale value immediately, and let exactly one request win a DynamoDB conditional-write lock to refresh it in the background. AirNow must see at most one call per location per TTL regardless of client concurrency. Cold-start-of-the-world (no entry at all) may block -- that's a once-per-location event. Cache TTL should align to AirNow's hourly publish schedule rather than being a rolling hour from first request.
close_reason: Implemented stale-while-revalidate + single-flight via Cache.get_stale(), Cache.try_acquire_refresh_lock() (DynamoDB conditional UpdateItem), and TTL alignment to the next boundary since epoch (cache.seconds_until_next_boundary()) rather than a rolling window. Two real concurrency bugs found and fixed via live testing under genuine thread/process concurrency (not just simulated-lock unit tests): (1) Cache.put() used PutItem which wiped the lock attribute early, letting a slower request acquire a fresh lock and redundantly re-fetch -- fixed by switching to UpdateItem touching only Data/FetchedAt/ExpiresAt. (2) A TOCTOU race between a request's own miss-check and its own lock-acquisition -- fixed by re-checking the cache immediately after winning the lock. Also fixed bin/run_local.py to use ThreadingHTTPServer instead of the single-connection HTTPServer, since the latter made it impossible to observe real concurrent-request behavior locally at all. Added the missing dynamodb:UpdateItem IAM permission to template.yaml. Verified live at 10 and 20 genuinely concurrent requests against real AirNow: exactly one AirNow call per batch each time. 57/57 tests pass, pylint 10.00/10, sam validate --lint clean.

description: A thin script (Flask or plain http.server/wsgiref) serves the same core handler logic over HTTP on localhost -- e.g. 'make run-local' or 'python bin/run_local.py'. No Docker, no SAM CLI, no AWS deploy required to test manually. Reads the AirNow key from a local env var/.env file, not Secrets Manager/SSM, so nothing about local dev touches AWS.
notes: Correction: same shell quoting bug as q9r.11's close reason -- 'so  needs no manual env setup' should read 'so `make run-local` needs no manual env setup'. No functional impact, just a typo in the record.

title: Define shared models: AQIReading, PollutantReading, Location
description:
Common models both data-source clients decode into, so callers don't care which source answered.

MUST include the official EPA AQI category table as a single shared mapping -- not left for each UI target to define separately. Values below are verbatim from the AQI Technical Assistance Document (EPA 454/B-18-007, Sept 2018), Tables 1 and 2. These are binding by incorporation: the AirNow Data Exchange Guidelines require values be 'disseminated in accordance with the AQI and corresponding RGB colors as directed in the Technical Assistance Document.'

  RANGE      DESCRIPTOR                      COLOR    RGB            HEX
  0-50       Good                            Green    0, 228, 0      #00E400
  51-100     Moderate                        Yellow   255, 255, 0    #FFFF00
  101-150    Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups  Orange   255, 126, 0    #FF7E00
  151-200    Unhealthy                       Red      255, 0, 0      #FF0000
  201-300    Very Unhealthy                  Purple   143, 63, 151   #8F3F97
  301-500    Hazardous                       Maroon   126, 0, 35     #7E0023

Full descriptor is 'Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups'; 'USG' is AirNow's own abbreviation for tight layouts (seen on airnow.gov's legend) and is acceptable where space genuinely requires it.

AQI values above 500 are 'Beyond the AQI' and need separate handling -- see bluegull-aqi-10h.16. See doc/DESIGN.md 'AQI Technical Assistance Document & API Fact Sheet -- review findings'.

title: Label displayed values as NowCast, not a spot reading
description:
AirNow's real-time observations are NowCast AQI -- EPA's endorsed method for relating short-term data to the AQI. It uses a VARIABLE averaging window: longer when air quality is stable, shorter when changing fast (PM2.5 ~12h stable / ~3h variable; ozone ~8h stable / ~1h variable).

So the number is a weighted average designed to track lived experience -- NOT an instantaneous sensor reading, and NOT the daily AQI (which requires a full 24 hours and is what agencies report for 'yesterday'). UI copy must not imply otherwise: avoid phrasing like 'right now' or 'current reading' that suggests a spot measurement.

'Current Air Quality' is the phrasing airnow.gov itself uses and is safe. This is a copy/labeling task, plus deciding whether to surface a brief explanation of NowCast somewhere reachable (natural fit alongside the preliminary-data disclaimer in the popover/expand view). See doc/DESIGN.md 'What the number is: NowCast, not a spot reading'.

title: Handle AQI > 500 (beyond the AQI scale) as valid data
description:
The category model currently has no representation for AQI above 500, so the default behavior is a blank/unknown category -- which would black out the app during exactly the conditions that produce such readings. That is the failure mode to design against.

RESOLVED: >500 is rare but REAL DATA, not an error.
  - TAD Table 1 bounds Hazardous at 301-500; above that is 'Beyond the AQI', where a value 'can still be computed to indicate relative magnitude' using the Hazardous breakpoints, and users should 'follow the recommendations for the Hazardous category'. NowCast handles it no differently. EPA would not document a computation for something that could only be a fault.
  - It has actually occurred in official reporting: Oregon DEQ recorded Bend above 500 on 2020-09-12 ('beyond the AQI scale' in their words), Newport 'well over 500', during that September's wildfires.
  - We never compute AQI (bluegull-aqi-10h.17), so anything received has already passed AirNow's own QA. Data trustworthiness is upstream of us; our obligation is to disseminate as received.

EARLIER ERROR CORRECTED: a previous version of this issue claimed airnow.gov diverged from the TAD by showing '301 +'. Wrong -- that came from a collapsed text extraction. The expanded AQI Legend panel shows '301 - 500  Hazardous' plus 'Values above 500 are beyond the AQI scale'. Both sources agree; there is no conflict to resolve.

IMPLEMENT: display the actual value; keep maroon (#7E0023) and the Hazardous health guidance per the TAD's explicit direction; indicate it is beyond the scale, using AirNow's own phrasing ('Values above 500 are beyond the AQI scale') rather than inventing wording. Do NOT clamp to 500 -- that would misrepresent the reading and conflicts with 'disseminated as received'.

SEPARATE CONCERN, handle distinctly: genuinely malformed values -- negative AQI, non-numeric, absurd magnitudes -- indicate a parse or transport fault rather than extreme air, and belong in an error state, not the beyond-the-scale path. Don't conflate the two.

Test with a fixture at e.g. AQI 650 to confirm it renders correctly rather than blanking.
close_reason: Fixed a real conflation bug: negative AQI (malformed data) previously fell through the same default case as >500 (real beyond-the-scale data), silently misclassifying corrupted input as extreme air quality. AQICategory.init(aqi:) is now failable, returning nil for negative input; PollutantReading.category updated to flatMap accordingly. Added isBeyondScale and beyondScaleNotice (AirNow's own verbatim phrasing 'Values above 500 are beyond the AQI scale', not invented wording). Deliberately did not add upper-bound implausibility detection -- disseminating AirNow's data as received (10h.17) means not second-guessing magnitude past the one unambiguous boundary (negative). Tested with AQI 650 (matching the real Oregon DEQ 2020 wildfire historical example cited in this issue) confirming it renders as valid data, not blank. 22/22 tests pass via swift test.

title: Bound App Group cache retention and review file protection
description: The App Group container holds the user's location history on disk -- the locations matter considerably more than the AQI values do. Bound retention rather than accumulating indefinitely, and review the file protection class on the container.
close_reason: Found a real gap: original AppGroupCache.get() treated an expired entry as a miss but never deleted it, so stale entries accumulated forever, and since cleanup only fired reactively on a get() for that exact key, a never-revisited location would never get cleaned up. Fixed with two mechanisms: (1) expired entries deleted both reactively on get() and proactively across every entry on each put(). (2) hard cap on entry count (maxRetainedEntries=10), evicting oldest-by-fetchedAt when exceeded -- TTL alone only bounds age not count. Added SharedCacheStore.allKeys() so AppGroupCache can enumerate/sweep its own prefixed entries without touching a shared store's other data. title: Configure Route53 + ACM custom domain in template.yaml
description:
DECIDED 2026-07-28: three stacks, one hosted zone. Prod = bare aqi.bluegull.org. Dev = dev.aqi.bluegull.org. Staging = stage.aqi.bluegull.org. All three are dot-subdomains of aqi.bluegull.org, so all covered by the single Route53 hosted zone delegated from bluegull.org's existing DNS (which lives elsewhere and stays there) -- one NS delegation covers all three environments, no per-environment delegation needed. Hosted zone in AWS account 843088391598.

(First pass used hyphenated names dev-aqi.bluegull.org/stage-aqi.bluegull.org, which turn out to be DNS SIBLINGS of aqi.bluegull.org rather than subdomains -- a hosted zone for aqi.bluegull.org can't contain them. Reconsidered to dot-subdomains specifically to keep the single-delegation approach.)

Route53 hosted zone + ACM cert(s), DNS-validated once delegation propagates. Matches Plant-Tracer's ${StackName}.${BaseDomain} naming pattern in template.yaml exactly, and its per-environment deploy-dev/deploy-demo/deploy-production split (currently -OFF there) -- see bluegull-aqi-q9r.8.
notes:
bluegull.org is registered with Squarespace -- that's where the NS delegation record for 'aqi' gets added (Squarespace domain panel: Settings > Domains > bluegull.org > DNS Settings, add a Custom record: Type NS, Host 'aqi', pointing to the 4 nameservers Route53 generates when the aqi.bluegull.org hosted zone is created). Squarespace's own DNS for the rest of bluegull.org is untouched.
CORRECTED delegation steps (sourced from Squarespace's own help article, 2026-07-28 -- prior notes here were an unverified guess and were wrong): Domains dashboard -> click bluegull.org -> DNS -> DNS Settings -> scroll to Custom Records -> Add record -> Type: NS, Name: 'aqi' (Squarespace appends .bluegull.org automatically), Nameserver: one AWS hostname (e.g. ns-1234.awsdns-12.com) -- a HOSTNAME, not an IP. Needs 4 separate rows, one per Route53-assigned nameserver, all with Name 'aqi'. PREREQUISITE: DNSSEC must be disabled first (Domains dashboard > bluegull.org > DNS > DNSSEC > toggle off). Changes take 24-48 hours per Squarespace. Source: https://support.squarespace.com/hc/en-us/articles/31093649681037-Adding-NS-records-to-subdomains
Trailing dot on AWS-provided nameserver hostnames (e.g. 'ns-1234.awsdns-12.com.'): STRIP IT before pasting into Squarespace's Nameserver field -- enter 'ns-1234.awsdns-12.com' without the trailing dot. Reasoning, not a sourced confirmation (Squarespace's docs give no example format): the trailing dot is zone-file FQDN-root notation, which is how Route53's console displays it, but consumer DNS panel form fields conventionally expect the hostname without it and may fail validation on the literal dot. If Squarespace rejects the no-dot form, try with the dot as fallback.
DELEGATION CONFIRMED LIVE 2026-07-28: dig NS aqi.bluegull.org +short returns the 4 expected awsdns nameservers (ns-532.awsdns-02.net, ns-1312.awsdns-36.org, ns-155.awsdns-19.com, ns-1954.awsdns-52.co.uk). Squarespace's NS-record UI (Custom Records, no trailing dot per prior note) worked as configured -- no DNSSEC or trailing-dot issue in the end. ACM DNS validation for a cert on aqi.bluegull.org (and the dev./stage. subdomains once those hosted-zone records exist) can now proceed.
Region decided: us-east-2 (cost, not Plant-Tracer's us-east-1). No conflict: AWS::Serverless::HttpApi custom domains are regional-only (unlike REST API v1's edge-optimized option, which forces the cert into us-east-1 regardless of API region) -- so the ACM cert for aqi.bluegull.org just needs to be requested in us-east-2, matching wherever the HttpApi itself deploys.

title: Evaluate CloudFront in front of the API
description:
Deliberately deferred, not rejected. The response is identical for everyone in a region and changes hourly -- close to an ideal CDN workload. CloudFront would absorb most traffic at the edge before it reaches Lambda, cutting cost and attack surface together, and offers better DDoS absorption than raw API Gateway. REGION GOTCHA if this is ever picked up: the API itself deploys to us-east-2, but CloudFront's ACM certificate MUST be requested in us-east-1 specifically -- a hard, non-negotiable CloudFront-wide rule, completely independent of which region the origin (API Gateway) runs in. title: Display sensitive groups and cautionary statements (POST-v1)
description:
DEFERRED past v1 -- decided 2026-07-28. Not a rejection: the content is valuable and the task stays open, just not in the first release.

TAD Table 3 (pollutant-specific sensitive groups) and Table 4 (cautionary statements per pollutant per AQI category) supply authoritative health-guidance text -- e.g. for PM2.5 at Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups: 'People with heart or lung disease, older adults, children, and people of lower socioeconomic status should reduce prolonged or heavy exertion.'

NOT REQUIRED OF US: those are reporting obligations on agencies when AQI > 100, and we are a downstream redistributor, not a reporting agency. That is what makes deferring it defensible -- v1 ships compliant without it. (Compare the attribution and preliminary-data disclaimer tasks, which ARE obligations and gate App Store submission.)

WHEN PICKED UP -- first check whether the AirNow API already returns this text (it may, via health-message or action-day fields). Displaying what the API returns is strongly preferable to embedding TAD table text: it stays current if EPA revises the language, and it honors 'disseminated as received'. If we do embed TAD text, it must be verbatim and unaltered.

Natural home is the post-v1 richer detail view (bluegull-aqi-mtm.15) rather than the v1 expand view, which is deliberately scoped to compliance content only. Note the app's health-protective purpose argues for this eventually -- the TAD states the AQI exists 'to inform people about their air quality so they can take steps to protect their health', especially above AQI 100.

title: Expand widget detail view with richer API data (POST-v1)
description:
DEFERRED -- explicitly not for the first release. Steve's framing: 'good scope creep... defer it.'

Once bluegull-aqi-mtm.14 exists (tap-to-expand -> detail view, v1 scope: attribution + disclaimer only), that same view is a natural place to show meaningfully more than the widget face does -- more like Apple Weather's expanded view (trends, forecast, additional pollutant detail, historical data) than a compliance-only screen. Deliberately unspecced beyond that for now; flesh out scope when it's actually picked up post-v1, informed by whatever AirNow endpoints (e.g. forecast, which the v1 data-scope decision chose not to fetch) seem worth adding at that point.

title: Investigate App Attest support on native macOS
description: UNVERIFIED: App Attest / DeviceCheck is well-established on iOS, but native macOS support is unconfirmed. If supported, it is the real answer to 'only our app may call this API' and would meaningfully change the abuse picture for an otherwise unauthenticated public endpoint. Do NOT design around it until confirmed. Research task only -- outcome is a yes/no plus a sketch of what adopting it would require.
close_reason: Resolved: App Attest IS supported on native macOS as of macOS 27 (previously unsupported -- isSupported reliably returned false even with a Secure Enclave). Extension-type restriction (main app + Action/SSO only, not WidgetKit extensions) turns out not to matter here since the widget extension never makes its own network calls. Requires full security mode + SIP on macOS. Documented the adoption sketch (client attestation ceremony + per-request assertions; server-side verification against Apple's root cert chain + replay tracking, a real new backend feature) in doc/DESIGN.md; not implemented -- adopting it means raising the min supported OS to 27, a scope decision for later.

title: Consider branch protection on main (PR-only merges)
description:
DEFERRED 2026-07-27 as premature -- with no code and no CI yet, branch protection is friction without benefit. Revisit when there is a real branch workflow or something worth gating review on, which naturally coincides with CI existing and producing status checks to require.

Decisions still open when this is picked up:
  - enforce_admins: should the rule bind the repo owner too (strong guarantee, deliberate friction for emergency pushes) or allow admin bypass (advisory only, since the owner is currently the sole committer)?

Already settled:
  - Required approving reviews must be 0. GitHub does not permit approving your own PR, so requiring 1 on a solo repo makes every merge impossible without a second account or an admin bypass.
  - Also block force-push and deletion on main.
  - Required status checks are the main source of value here; add them once CI workflows exist.

Verify afterward that 'bd dolt push' still works. Beads syncs to refs/dolt/data, which is outside refs/heads/ and should be unaffected by a main branch rule -- but confirm rather than assume.

title: Investigate whether a CLI exists to force an installed widget timeline reload
description: Unverified assumption flagged in doc/DESIGN.md: it is not known whether a supported command-line tool can force an installed widget to reload its timeline (as opposed to WidgetCenter.reloadAllTimelines() called from app code). Nothing in the plan depends on it -- this is a nice-to-have that would tighten the manual background-refresh verification loop. Confirm before relying on it; do not assume it exists.
close_reason: Resolved: no supported CLI exists to force a real Mac's installed widget to reload its timeline. WidgetCenter.reloadAllTimelines()/reloadTimelines(ofKind:) from app code remain the only sanctioned path; simctl's widget support is iOS-Simulator-only. Found the common killall NotificationCenter workaround but it's unsupported/undocumented and system-wide, not fit for verification tooling. Practical finding: the Xcode debugger removes WidgetKit's normal reload throttling entirely, so debugger-attached manual testing is the real way to tighten the loop. Documented in doc/DESIGN.md.
